label: new_skill

expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: "**Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**"

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: The briefing has labeled sections "**Key debates**", "**Major voices.**", "**Patterns**" and "**Open questions.**", plus a Background section.

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: Counting from Background through Open questions gives about 450 words, which is inside the 300–500 range.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved an interactive map of six possible angles. Open this file in your browser: .../mind-map.html"

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The reply says there are six angles. Each visible branch has 2–3 children, and every angle has a 0–1 value, e.g. "saturation": 0.85 with 3 children and "District budgets" 0.5 with 2 children. The last branches are cut off in the file excerpt.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: Every label is a short topic, e.g. "Student achievement", "Hourly support staff", "What teachers do on the fifth day". None is phrased as a question.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: "which direction interests you most, and why?" The reply does not recommend any angle.

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count. Links and DOIs in the mind map count too.
expectations.evidence: Each link was fetched: the two edweek pages, journalistsresource, pmc PMC9979633, econpapers 10.1086/712916 and ideas.repec v64y2018icp31-39. The reply cites no DOIs that weren't opened.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "which direction interests you most, and why?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: There are two questions: "what are your current thoughts on four-day weeks..." and "which direction interests you most, and why?". "ask me how I know it" is an invitation, not a question.
